card.name: Noh
card.era: Mid-14th century (developed by Kan'ami and Zeami)
card.tagline: Oldest surviving Japanese masked dance-drama theatre
card.profile: Noh is a major form of classical Japanese dance-drama performed since the 14th century, developed by Kan'ami and his son Zeami, and is the oldest major theatre art still regularly performed (Wikipedia). It integrates masks, costumes and props in a dance-based performance requiring highly trained actors and musicians; the dance element is the mai (Wikipedia). Often based on traditional literature, its hero is frequently a supernatural being in human form narrating a story (UNESCO). Together with the comic kyogen it forms nogaku, proclaimed a UNESCO Masterpiece in 2001 and inscribed on the Representative List in 2008 as 'Nogaku theatre' (UNESCO).
card.insight: Per Wikipedia, Noh masks are carved from blocks of Japanese cypress and there are 'approximately 450 different masks mostly based on sixty types, all of which have distinctive names,' each conveying shifting emotion through the actor's movement (Wikipedia).
